senses.def: not being used or lived in; empty
ex: There are no vacant rooms in the hotel.
The seat next to me was vacant.

senses.def: showing no interest or thought
ex: He gave me a vacant stare.

senses.def: a substance put into the body to protect it from a disease
ex: Scientists developed a vaccine against the virus.
Children receive a vaccine at school.

senses.def: not clear or exact
ex: He gave a vague answer.
I have only a vague memory of that day.

senses.def: too proud of your own appearance or abilities
ex: He is a vain man who loves looking in mirrors.

senses.def: in vain: without success
ex: They searched in vain for the missing keys.

senses.def: a card sent to someone you love on 14 February
ex: He sent her a valentine signed with a question mark.

senses.def: the person you send a love card to
ex: Will you be my valentine?

senses.def: officially acceptable, especially for a fixed period
ex: Your passport must be valid for six months.
The ticket is valid until Friday.

senses.def: based on good reasons and able to be accepted
ex: She made a valid point about the cost.

senses.def: an area of low land between hills or mountains, often with a river
ex: The village lies in a green valley.
A river runs through the valley.

senses.def: worth a lot of money
ex: Please leave your valuable items in the hotel safe.
The painting is extremely valuable.

senses.def: very useful or important
ex: Thank you for your valuable advice.
The trip was a valuable experience.

senses.def: the amount of money that something is worth
ex: The value of the house has doubled.
This car is good value for money.

senses.def: values: the beliefs about what is right and important in life
ex: Honesty is one of our family values.

senses.def: to think that something is important or useful
ex: I value your honesty.
She values her free time.

senses.def: a covered road vehicle, smaller than a lorry, used for carrying goods
ex: A delivery van stopped outside the shop.
They loaded the furniture into the van.

senses.def: a person who damages public property on purpose
ex: Vandals broke the windows of the school.
Vandals sprayed paint on the bus shelter.

senses.def: to disappear suddenly or completely
ex: The thief vanished into the crowd.
His smile vanished when he saw the bill.

senses.def: too much pride in your own appearance or achievements
ex: His vanity made it hard for him to accept advice.

senses.def: a bathroom cupboard with a basin set into the top
ex: The vanity in the bathroom has two drawers.

senses.def: a number of different kinds of the same thing
ex: The shop sells a wide variety of cheese.
I like a bit of variety in my work.

senses.def: a particular type of something
ex: This variety of apple is very sweet.

senses.def: several different
ex: She has lived in various countries.
The shop sells various kinds of bread.

senses.def: extremely large in size or amount
ex: The desert is a vast area of sand.
A vast number of people watched the match.

senses.def: not eating or containing meat or fish
ex: We ordered a vegetarian pizza.
My sister has been vegetarian for years.

senses.def: a person who does not eat meat or fish
ex: Are there any dishes for vegetarians?

senses.def: plants in general, especially those growing in a particular area
ex: Thick vegetation covered the hillside.
Desert vegetation needs very little water.

senses.def: a machine, such as a car or bus, that carries people or goods on land
ex: Heavy vehicles are not allowed on the bridge.
The police stopped the vehicle.

senses.def: a way of expressing ideas or achieving something
ex: The magazine is a vehicle for new writers.

senses.def: one of the tubes that carry blood to the heart
ex: The nurse found a vein in my arm.
The veins in his neck were visible.

senses.def: a particular style or mood in writing or talking
ex: He continued in the same humorous vein.

senses.def: producing poison that can hurt or kill when it bites or stings
ex: Some snakes in the area are highly venomous.
The venomous spider hid in the shoe.

senses.def: full of anger and hate
ex: He sent a venomous reply.

senses.def: the movement of fresh air into and around a room or building
ex: The kitchen needs better ventilation.
The room had no ventilation at all.

senses.def: a new business activity or project that involves risk
ex: His first business venture failed.
They started a joint venture with a Japanese firm.

senses.def: a place where an event such as a concert or meeting is held
ex: The wedding venue was a beautiful garden.
The concert venue holds five thousand people.

senses.def: spoken, not written
ex: They made a verbal agreement.
She gave a verbal warning to the staff.

senses.def: connected with words and the use of language
ex: The test checks verbal and number skills.

senses.def: using exactly the same words as were originally used
ex: The newspaper printed a verbatim report of the speech.

senses.def: in exactly the same words
ex: She repeated his words verbatim.

senses.def: an official decision in a court of law about whether someone is guilty
ex: The jury reached a verdict of not guilty.
We are waiting for the verdict.

senses.def: an opinion after considering something
ex: What's your verdict on the new restaurant?

senses.def: truly; used in old or religious language
ex: Verily, I say unto you, the day will come.

senses.def: used to emphasise that you think something can be properly described by a strong word
ex: The garden was a veritable paradise.
He is a veritable genius with numbers.

senses.def: small animals, such as rats, that carry disease or damage crops
ex: The farmer put out traps to catch vermin.
The old building was full of vermin.

senses.def: able to do many different things, or to be used in many ways
ex: Rice is a versatile food.
She is a versatile actor who can play any role.

senses.def: writing in lines with a rhythm, as in poetry
ex: He wrote a book of humorous verse.

senses.def: one of the parts that a song or poem is divided into
ex: The children sang the first verse of the song.

senses.def: to compete against someone in a game (informal)
ex: Our school will verse theirs on Saturday.

senses.def: a particular form of something that is slightly different from other forms
ex: I prefer the original version of the film.
The latest version of the app is faster.

senses.def: one person's description of an event
ex: The two witnesses gave different versions of the accident.

senses.def: used to show two sides in a competition or in a choice
ex: Tonight's match is Spain versus Brazil.
It's a case of quality versus price.

senses.def: standing straight up at an angle of 90 degrees to the ground
ex: The wall was almost vertical.
Draw a vertical line down the page.

senses.def: used before an adjective or adverb to make it stronger
ex: The soup is very hot.
She speaks very quickly.

senses.def: used to emphasise an exact point, time or thing
ex: This is the very place where we met.
At that very moment, the phone rang.

mistake.note: Very cannot be used before a verb; use really or very much instead.

senses.def: a ship or large boat
ex: The vessel sailed from the port at dawn.
A fishing vessel was lost at sea.

senses.def: a container for liquids
ex: The vessel was filled with olive oil.

senses.def: a tube that carries blood in the body
ex: Blood vessels carry blood around the body.

senses.def: a doctor who treats sick or injured animals
ex: We took the cat to the vet.
She wants to become a vet.

senses.def: a person with a lot of experience in a particular activity
ex: He is a veteran of the film industry.

senses.def: a person who has served in the armed forces, especially in a war
ex: The veterans marched through the city.

senses.def: going through a place on the way to somewhere else
ex: We flew to Cairo via Dubai.

senses.def: by means of; using
ex: You can book tickets via our website.

senses.def: used in titles for someone who is second in rank and can act for the leader
ex: She is the vice president of the company.
The vice captain led the team.

senses.def: the area near a particular place
ex: There are no shops in the vicinity of the hotel.
The police searched the vicinity.

senses.def: cruel and violent, with a wish to hurt
ex: The dog gave him a vicious bite.
It was a vicious attack.

senses.def: intended to hurt someone's feelings
ex: She spread vicious rumours about him.

senses.def: a person who has been hurt, killed or badly treated
ex: The victims of the flood need food and shelter.
He was a victim of crime.

senses.def: having won a victory
ex: The victorious team celebrated in the street.
She emerged victorious from the contest.

senses.def: success in winning a game, battle or competition
ex: The team celebrated their victory.
He won a great victory in the election.

senses.def: everything that you can see from a particular place
ex: Our room has a lovely view of the sea.
The view from the top was beautiful.

senses.def: an opinion or belief
ex: What is your view on this problem?
In my view, he is right.

senses.def: to look at something carefully
ex: Visitors can view the paintings from ten o'clock.
You can view your account online.

senses.def: to think about something in a particular way
ex: Many people view the plan as a mistake.

senses.def: a large house, especially one used for holidays
ex: We rented a villa near the beach.
The villa has a private swimming pool.

senses.def: a small group of houses and other buildings in the countryside
ex: She grew up in a small village.
There is a shop in the village.

senses.def: proof that something you did or said was right
ex: The results were a vindication of her theory.
His success was a vindication of his hard work.

senses.def: a sour liquid used to add flavour to food or to preserve it
ex: Add a little vinegar to the salad.
The pickles are stored in vinegar.

senses.def: to break a law, rule or agreement
ex: The company violated safety rules.
The soldiers violated the ceasefire.

senses.def: to disturb or fail to respect something private or peaceful
ex: The photos violated her privacy.

senses.def: behaviour that is intended to hurt or kill people
ex: The film contains scenes of violence.
The police tried to stop the violence.

senses.def: using force to hurt or kill people
ex: He was arrested for a violent attack.
I don't like violent films.

senses.def: very strong and sudden
ex: A violent storm hit the coast.

senses.def: having a blue-purple colour
ex: She wore a violet dress.
The sky turned violet at sunset.

senses.def: pure, clean or untouched, like someone who has never had sex
ex: The mountain was covered in virginal snow.

senses.def: made, done or seen on a computer or the internet rather than in real life
ex: We took a virtual tour of the museum.
The company holds virtual meetings every week.

senses.def: almost the thing described
ex: The two companies have a virtual monopoly.

senses.def: almost; very nearly
ex: The streets were virtually empty.
The project is virtually finished.

senses.def: a good quality in someone's character
ex: Patience is a virtue.
Honesty was her greatest virtue.

senses.def: an advantage that makes something better
ex: The plan has the virtue of being cheap.

senses.def: a person who is extremely skilled, especially at playing music
ex: The violin virtuoso played to a full hall.

senses.def: a very small living thing that causes illness
ex: The flu virus spreads quickly in winter.
Doctors are studying the new virus.

senses.def: a harmful program that damages computer files
ex: A virus deleted all my files.

senses.def: an official document or stamp in a passport that allows you to enter or stay in a country
ex: I need a visa to visit that country.
Her visa expires next month.

senses.def: able to be seen
ex: The mountains are visible from my window.
The scar is barely visible.

senses.def: the ability to see
ex: He has poor vision in one eye.

senses.def: an idea of what something could be like in the future
ex: The leader has a clear vision for the country.

senses.def: relating to seeing or to things that you look at
ex: The teacher used visual aids such as pictures.
Painting is a visual art.

senses.def: extremely important and necessary
ex: Water is vital for life.
It is vital that you arrive on time.

senses.def: energy and enthusiasm
ex: The old man still has great vitality.
The new shops gave the town new vitality.

senses.def: a natural substance in food that the body needs to stay healthy
ex: Oranges are rich in vitamin C.
She takes vitamins every morning.

senses.def: relating to the skills needed for a particular job or career
ex: He is taking a vocational course in plumbing.
Vocational training helps young people find work.

senses.def: the sound that you make when you speak or sing
ex: She has a beautiful singing voice.
Please keep your voice down.

senses.def: the right or chance to give your opinion
ex: Everyone should have a voice in the decision.

senses.def: to say what you think or feel
ex: Many parents voiced concerns about safety.

senses.def: a mountain with an opening through which hot melted rock, gas and ash can burst out
ex: The volcano erupted last night.
Tourists climb the volcano in summer.

senses.def: the loudness of a sound
ex: Please turn down the volume.
The TV volume was too high.

senses.def: the amount of something, or the space inside an object
ex: The volume of traffic has doubled.
The tank has a volume of 50 litres.

senses.def: one book in a set of books
ex: The encyclopedia has twenty volumes.

senses.def: in a way that you choose to do, not because you are forced
ex: She left the job voluntarily.
He voluntarily gave the police his phone.

senses.def: done because you choose to, not because you must
ex: Attendance at the meeting is voluntary.
She does voluntary work at a hospital.

senses.def: to offer to do something without being asked or paid
ex: She volunteered to help at the school fair.
He volunteers at an animal shelter.

senses.def: a person who does a job willingly without being paid
ex: Volunteers cleaned the beach on Sunday.
We need more volunteers.

senses.def: food or liquid from the stomach that comes out through the mouth
ex: The floor was covered in vomit.

senses.def: a fast-spinning mass of water or air that pulls things into its centre
ex: The boat was pulled into a vortex of water.

senses.def: a situation that you cannot escape from
ex: He was drawn into a vortex of debt.

senses.def: a serious promise
ex: They exchanged wedding vows.
He made a vow to stop smoking.

senses.def: a long journey, especially by sea or in space
ex: The voyage across the ocean took two weeks.
They went on a voyage to the Arctic.
